  MEETING MINUTES
  Thursday, November 19, 2024
  an Dimas  enior Citizen/ Community Center
  Meeting Room
  201 E. Bonita Avenue

 1.  Call to Order and Flag Salute
  The Parks and Recreation Commission meeting was called to order at 6: 00 p. m.

  Brandon [Toon, Commissioner
  Edward Rodriguez, Vice Chair
  Christina Tsang, Commissioner
  Scott Wasserman, Parks & Recreation Director
  Joseph Jones, RecreationManager
  Shari Garwick, Director of Public Works
  Lauren Marshall, Public Works Sr. Management Analyst
  Connie Arellano, Management Aide

E, •

  Commissioner Ash moved to approve the minutes of the September 17, 2024
  Parks and Recreation Commission meeting, seconded by Vice Chair Rodriguez
  w

  and approved unanimously.

  a.  Director' s Report

  Mr. Wasserman provided updates on the following items:
  Upcoming budget deficit projection has received some relief from
  interest rates increasing it generated revenue for the City.
  City Council has been presented with San Dimas Recreation
  Center revenue and services to prioritize swim lessons and BUSD
  programming.
 Parks &  Recreation  Commission  Minutes
November  19, 2024

  Horsethief Canyon Park updates included the soccer field lighting
  completed; the walking trail in progress and soccer field renovation
  pending.
  City Council will be reviewing field reservation policies and special
  event for updates.

  Cost is under review for conversion of a tennis court to a pickleball
  court at Lone Hill Park due to proximity to homes.

  b. Recreation  Manager

  Mr. Jones handed out and reviewed the Recreation Division Report that
  included the 5K event with new location change; Halloween Trunk o Treat
  with a line of people that extended to 15t Street/ lglesia street; Bowser
  Bash at Horsethief Canyon Park and the Holiday Extravaganza and
  parade updates scheduled to be December 7t"

  Chair Bartolo requested information on the Holiday residential decorations
  judging for the Commission, Mr. Jones will provide updates to the
  Commission once details finalized.

  Vice Chair Rodriguez commented on his experience at the Halloween
  event and the line at the Haunted Hall maze moved quickly and was well
  organized.

6.  New Business

  Mr. Wasserman introduced the stormwater design project outreach efforts that
  discussions originally began in 2022.

  a. Sr. Management Analyst, Lauren Marshall discussed and presented the Lone
  Hill Park Stormwater Design project presentation and the public outreach
  results. Mrs. Marshall is asking Commission to provide input on the above
  ground park amenities.

  Mrs. Garwick elaborated on the drain infiltration issues throughout the City and
  once funding becomes available the next stage of construction will begin.
  Currently only designing is available to establish costs.

  Mr. Wasserman present the motion for Commission to vote on the top amenities
  recommendations for City Council to consider.

  Vice Chair Rodriguez moved to approve a playground as the first priority amenity
  and a basketball court as second amenity priority, seconded by Commissioner
  Ash and approved unanimously.

  b.  Recreation Experiences Available to Home Schooled Residents discussion.

  Chair Bartolo commented on the increased amount of interest and popularity in
  homeschooling children. Chair Bartolo stated that the homeschooling program
  offers parents an opportunity to enroll children in extracurricular activities, for
  instance dance, athletic and home economic classes using vouchers to enroll
  and asked if the Parks &  Recreation department or any other
  organization/ businesses in the City accept the vouchers or more details on the
  program.

  Ms. Arellano provided input on the homeschooling program currently offered by
  Charter schools who enroll as a vendor and the purchase order process to
  submit request for classes and invoice system to collect funds.

7.  Chair' s Report

  Chair Bartolo commented on the success of the Halloween event and also attended
  the San Dimas Heroes event on Veteran' s Day. Chair Bartolo asked if there was
  any participation for the Commission during the Holiday Extravaganza parade. Mr.
  Jones stated the parade was full and in the future the commission can enroll to be
  part of the parade lineup.

  Mr. Wasserman commented on the higher interest of equestrian community to
  participate in the parade.

  Commissioner Tsang was interested in judging the floats that were participating in
  the parade. Mr. Jones will send more details to commission to assist in judging.

8.  Commissioner' s Reports

  Commissioner Tsang reported on the 5K event experience with the staff and
  recommended for packets to be allowed to be picked at the same time of
  registration to assist with morning check -ins.

  Vice Chair Rodriguez provided an update on a special meeting attended that
  discussed the City pool and City Council considering of eliminating the pool facility.
  Vice Chair disagrees with getting rid of the pool as many community members grew
  up and learned to swim at the San Dimas Recreation Center and would like for
  Commission to agendize discussion of preserving the center or getting more
  revenue to save the City pool facility.

  Mr. Wasserman stated that there was a survey that went to community and
  discussion continues with Bonita Unified School District on the San Dimas
  Recreation Center and will add item in March when there is more direction or
  information from City Council on the subject.
